Tantalum is a chemical element; it has symbol Ta and atomic number 73.
What is the atomic number of Copper?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
In what year did Neil Armstrong die?
Neil Armstrong: Armstrong was born and raised near Wapakoneta, Ohio.
In what year was Methylphenidate discovered?
Methylphenidate: It may be taken by mouth or applied to the skin, and different formulations have varying durations of effect.
Which company manufactures TAI TF Kaan?
TAI TF Kaan: Turkish Aerospace Industries. Designed to replace the Turkish Air Force’s fleet of F-16 Fighting Falcons, the Kaan is also intended for export to international markets.
Chromium: Pfizer. Chromium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cr and atomic number 24.
In which country did the Hawker Siddeley Harrier take place?
Hawker Siddeley Harrier: United Kingdom. The Hawker Siddeley Harrier is a British jet-powered attack aircraft designed and produced by the British aerospace company Hawker Siddeley.
Who is credited with discovering Meitnerium?
GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research
Meitnerium: GSI Helmholtz Centre for Heavy Ion Research. Meitnerium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mt and atomic number 109.
Who is credited with discovering Allergic rhinitis?
Allergic rhinitis: John Bostock. It is classified as a type I hypersensitivity reaction.
Who is credited with discovering SARS-CoV-2?
SARS-CoV-2: Zhang Jixian. The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
One of the very few semiaquatic vipers in the world, which venomous pit viper native to the southeastern United States is often found coiled near slow-moving lakes, streams, and marshes?
Agkistrodon piscivorus is a species of venomous snake, a pit viper in the subfamily Crotalinae of the family Viperidae.
This group of large, semiaquatic boas native to tropical South America includes the green species, among the largest snakes on Earth — name the group?
Anaconda are a group of large boas of the genus Eunectes.
This discipline studies past human activity by recovering and analyzing artifacts, architecture, and other material remains through surveying and excavation — name the field?
Archaeology is the study of human activity through the recovery and analysis of material culture.
Born in 1655, this Italian instrument maker earned lasting fame for inventing a keyboard instrument that could play both soft and loud — who was he?
Bartolomeo Cristofori (Italian; May 4, 1655 - January 27, 1731) was an Italian maker of musical instruments famous for inventing the piano.
Caused by a recessive allele in the leopard but a dominant one in the jaguar, this dark melanistic variant still secretly carries its usual rosettes — what is it called?
Black panther is the melanistic colour variant of the leopard (Panthera pardus) and the jaguar (Panthera onca).

This shield-shaped insect, native to East Asia, was accidentally introduced to Allentown, Pennsylvania in 1998 and became a major agricultural pest feeding on over 100 plant species — what insect is it?
Brown marmorated stink bug (Halyomorpha halys) is an insect in the family Pentatomidae, native to China, Japan, Korea, and other Asian regions.

Once thought to not really exist as a stable molecule, this compound was confirmed since around 1990 to have a real, if fleeting, existence — lasting only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature — what compound is it?
Carbonic acid is a chemical compound with the chemical formula H2CO3.

This perennial flowering herb is the only species of its onion-relative genus native to both the New World and Old World, prized for its edible leaves and flowers and also used to repel insects. What herb is this?
Chives is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Part of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this loose-leafed member of the 'kale group' has been grown for its big, dark-green leaves since classical antiquity — what is it?
Collard (plant) is a group of loose-leafed cultivars of Brassica oleracea (the same species as many common vegetables, including cabbage and broccoli).
This breaded, deep-fried snack binds a thick sauce like béchamel with fillings such as meat, seafood, or cheese, and was originally a way to use up leftovers — what is it?
Croquette is a deep-fried roll originating in French cuisine and most extended in Spanish cuisine consisting of a thick binder combined with a filling, which is then breaded.
This annual herb in the celery family, native to North Africa and West Asia, is grown across Eurasia for both its feathery leaves and its seeds, both used to flavor food — what herb is it?
Dill (Anethum graveolens) is an annual herb in the celery family Apiaceae.
Sometimes occurring spontaneously during sleep as a nocturnal emission, this process involves the discharge of semen through the urethra — what is it called?
Ejaculation is the discharge of semen (the ejaculate; normally containing sperm) from the penis through the urethra.

Combining lab and field science with strong ties to ecology and evolutionary biology, this discipline earned three of its founders a shared 1973 Nobel Prize for their work on animal behavior — what field is it?
Ethology is a branch of zoology that studies the behaviour of non-human animals.
Using a skin membrane called a patagium plus a long tail for steering, these gliding rodents can sail from tree to tree without true flight — what are they called?
Flying squirrel (scientifically known as Pteromyini or Petauristini) are a tribe of 50 species of squirrels in the family Sciuridae.

A Belgian-British emigrant to New York, this inventor struck gold during a 1906 stay in Central America by perfecting an early instant-coffee process and building a company to mass-produce it — who was he?
George Washington (inventor) (May 20, 1871 - March 29, 1946) was a Belgian-British inventor and businessman.

This German physicist turned his eye on the mind itself, founding psychophysics and giving his name to a law showing that sensation rises with the logarithm — not the raw intensity — of a stimulus. Whose pioneering work was it?
Gustav Fechner (19 April 1801 - 18 November 1887) was a German physicist, philosopher, and experimental psychologist.
Sometimes called urticaria, this itchy rash of raised welts can flare for minutes or days, may follow an allergy or infection, and in half of all cases has no identifiable cause — what is it?
Hives is a kind of skin rash with red or flesh-colored, raised, itchy bumps.
First used ritually by forager tribes in Central Africa and later adopted by Gabon's Bwiti tradition, this psychoactive plant alkaloid interacts with both opioid and serotonin receptors — what is it?
Ibogaine is a psychoactive indole alkaloid derived from plants such as Tabernanthe iboga, characterized by hallucinogenic and oneirogenic effects.

This American scientist co-authored a landmark 1953 paper with Francis Crick proposing the double-helix structure of DNA, building on research by Rosalind Franklin, and shared a 1962 Nobel Prize for the discovery — who is he?
James Watson (April 6, 1928 - November 6, 2025) was an American molecular biologist, geneticist, and zoologist.
Cousin to the wallaby and wallaroo in the family Macropodidae, this Australian marsupial's biggest member is the red one. What is it?
Kangaroo are marsupials from the subfamily Macropodinae (macropods, meaning "large foot").

A hybrid of the citron and the bitter orange believed to have originated in northeastern India around the 1st millennium BC, this small evergreen citrus tree bears a tart yellow fruit used worldwide — name the fruit?
Lemon (Citrus limon) is a species of small evergreen tree in the Citrus genus of the flowering plant family Rutaceae.
Named for a Dutch physicist, this six-parameter family of linear equations converts spacetime coordinates between reference frames moving at constant relative velocity — what is it?
Lorentz transformation are a six-parameter family of linear transformations from a coordinate frame in spacetime to another frame that moves at a constant velocity relative to the former.

A student of Marie Curie, this French physicist discovered a new element in 1939 by purifying lanthanum laced with actinium, and went on to become the first woman elected to the French Académie des Sciences — who was she?
Marguerite Perey (19 October 1909 - 13 May 1975) was a French physicist and a student of Marie Curie.
Despite little formal education, this self-made English scientist established the concept of the electromagnetic field and uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction — who is he?
Michael Faraday (22 September 1791 - 25 August 1867) was an English chemist and physicist who contributed vastly to the study of electrochemistry and electromagnetism.

Though its 83 species can grow as tall as trees, this genus is technically herbaceous, its 'trunk' just tightly wrapped leaf stalks, and it gives us edible bananas, plantains, and fiber for cloth — what genus is it?
Musa (plant) is one of three genera in the family Musaceae.

First described in 1766 by naturalist Peter Simon Pallas, this sole living member of its genus sports a white throat patch and, in males only, a pair of short horns — what is this large Asian antelope called?
Nilgai (Boselaphus tragocamelus) (literally meaning "blue cow") is the largest antelope in Asia.
Named from the Greek word for 'smell,' this hard, brittle, bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and is often alloyed for fountain pen nib tips — which element?
Osmium (from Ancient Greek (osm) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.
Commercially produced from citrus fruits as a white-to-light-brown powder, this plant-cell-wall polysaccharide is the gelling agent that makes jams and jellies set — what is it?
Pectin (Ancient) is a heteropolysaccharide, a structural polymer contained in the cell walls and middle lamellae of terrestrial plants.
Confirming and popularizing Isaac Newton's work, this French scholar authored the five-volume 'Mécanique céleste' and helped pioneer the Bayesian view of probability — who is he?

Pierre-Simon Laplace (23 March 1749 - 5 March 1827) was a French polymath, a scholar whose work has been instrumental in the fields of physics, astronomy, mathematics, engineering, statistics, and philosophy.
A staple food across the world, this tuber is actually an underground stem from a plant in the nightshade family, with wild relatives growing from the southern U.S. all the way to Chile. What is it?
Potato is a starchy tuberous vegetable native to the Americas that is consumed as a staple food in many parts of the world.
Named partly for the Aztec feathered serpent god and partly for the designer of a tailless aircraft, this genus of giant pterosaur soared over Late Cretaceous North America — what is it?
Quetzalcoatlus is a genus of azhdarchid pterosaur that lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in North America.
One of the U.S. Air Force's three strategic bombers, this supersonic swing-wing aircraft hauls a 75,000-pound payload and answers to the affectionate name 'Bone' — what is it?
Rockwell B-1 Lancer is a supersonic variable-sweep wing, heavy bomber used by the United States Air Force.
Which genus of large, tropical, many-legged predators takes its name from ancient Greek words meaning roughly 'thorn' and 'earthworm'?
Scolopendra (from Ancient Greek (sklops), meaning "thorn", and (nteron), meaning "earthworm") is a species-rich genus of large tropical centipedes of the family Scolopendridae.
This vertebrate organ system serves three main functions, protection, regulation, and sensation, and in mammals is made of multiple layers of ectodermal tissue. What is it?

Skin is the layer of usually soft, flexible outer tissue covering the body of a vertebrate animal, with three main functions: protection, regulation, and sensation. The adjective cutaneous means "of the skin" (from Latin cutis 'skin').

Described as the most extreme form of malnutrition, this severe shortfall of caloric energy is so grave that deliberately inflicting it on a population is a crime under international law — what is it?
Starvation is a severe deficiency in caloric energy intake, below the level needed to maintain an organism's life.
This genus of flowering plants in the daisy family is better known by the fluffy-seeded lawn weed it produces, with two European species now invasive nearly worldwide. What is it?
Taraxacum is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae which consists of species commonly known as dandelions.
This intensely itchy, contagious fungal skin infection produces a red, scaly rash with a curved border across the groin and buttocks, mostly in men — what is it?

Tinea cruris (TC), also known as jock itch, is a common type of contagious, superficial fungal infection of the groin and buttocks region, which occurs predominantly but not exclusively in men and in hot-humid climates.
Medically called micturition or voiding, this voluntary process happens up to seven times a day in a healthy adult — and goes by "number one." What is it?
Urination is the release of urine from the bladder through the urethra in placental mammals, or through the cloaca in other vertebrates.
Intermediate in size between the Greyhound and the Italian Greyhound, this gentle, minimal-shedding sighthound turns into a bundle of energy the moment it's outdoors — which breed?
Whippet is a British breed of sighthound. It closely resembles the Greyhound and the smaller Italian Greyhound, and is intermediate between them in size.
This Danish physicist shared the 1975 Nobel for work on the structure of the atomic nucleus — making him and his famous father one of the rare parent-child pairs to each win the prize. Who was he?
Native to the arid Americas, most rosettes of this succulent genus flower gloriously just once before dying, earning one species the nickname 'century plant' — what genus is it?
Meaning 'different lizard' and first described in 1877 by Othniel Marsh, most fossils of this Late Jurassic predator come from North America's Morrison Formation — which dinosaur?

Found along the Andes and Pacific coasts of South America, this enormous New World vulture is one of the largest flying birds by wingspan, with males sporting a fleshy comb atop a bald red head — which species is it?
Andean condor: Species of bird. The Andean condor (Vultur gryphus) is a South American New World vulture and is the only extant member of the genus Vultur.
First described by Linnaeus in 1753, this Old World vegetable — better known on dinner plates as celery — is also cultivated for a bulbous root form called celeriac. What is its scientific name?

One of its founders, James Keeler, said this science 'seeks to ascertain the nature of the heavenly bodies... rather than their positions or motions' — studying everything from the Sun to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
Originating in Central Africa, this hunting dog breed doesn't bark but makes an unusual yodel-like sound instead, earning it a nickname — what breed is it?
Basenji: Central African breed of dog. The Fédération Cynologique Internationale places it in the Spitz and "primitive types" categories, while the American Kennel Club classifies it as a hound.
Also known as vitamin B7, this B vitamin is found in every living cell and is popularly sold as a supplement; isolated, it's a white needle-like crystal — what is it?
Biotin: Chemical compound and essential nutrient.

Completely dependent on humans for reproduction after millennia of selective breeding, this domesticated moth's caterpillars produce the raw fiber behind a 5,000-year-old Chinese industry — which species?
Bombyx mori: Moth mainly used in the production of silk.

Prescribed under the tongue, as a cheek film, an injection, a skin patch, or an implant, this opioid treats pain and opioid use disorder — often combined with naloxone in Suboxone to deter injection misuse. What is it?
Buprenorphine: Opioid used to treat pain and opioid use disorder.
This golden fungus — also known as 'girolle' — is often confused with a poisonous lookalike, though it remains a prized edible mushroom and the type species of its genus — which one is it?
Cantharellus cibarius: Species of fungus. Despite its characteristic features, C. cibarius can be confused with species such as the poisonous Omphalotus illudens.
Marketed as Zinacef and used against everything from meningitis to Lyme disease, this second-generation cephalosporin antibiotic was patented in 1971 — which drug?
Cefuroxime: Antibiotic medication. It is used by mouth or by injection into a vein or muscle.

Caused by a bacterium and often symptomless for weeks after exposure, this sexually transmitted infection can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility in women if untreated — which infection?
Chlamydia: Sexually transmitted bacterial infection. Chlamydia, or more specifically a chlamydia infection, is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis.

First discovered as an atypical antipsychotic, this medication is reserved for schizophrenia patients who haven't responded to two other drugs, and is also used for psychosis linked to Parkinson's disease — what is it?
Clozapine: Atypical antipsychotic medication. Clozapine, sold under the brand name Clozaril among others, is a psychiatric medication and was the first atypical antipsychotic to be discovered.
These wind-pollinated, cone-bearing evergreens dominated Earth's landscapes throughout the Mesozoic before flowering plants took over — what group of plants is this?
Conifer: Group of seed plants. As of 2025, 94 conifer species are listed as endangered and 30 as critically endangered.
This practice of secure communication sits at the intersection of math, computer science, and electrical engineering, and underpins e-commerce and chip-based payment cards — what is it called?
Cryptography: Practice and study of secure communication techniques.

Also nicknamed 'the bends,' this diving-related condition happens when dissolved gases form bubbles in body tissue during a too-rapid ascent, often settling painfully in the knees and elbows — what is it called?
Decompression sickness: Disorder caused by dissolved gases forming bubbles in tissues.

He didn't just arrange the known elements — he left gaps and boldly predicted the properties of three undiscovered ones, later vindicated by germanium, gallium, and scandium. Which Russian chemist was he?
Born in 1869 into an old Anglo-Irish scientific family in Dublin, she is considered the world's first woman medical physicist — who was she?
Edith Anne Stoney: Anglo-Irish medical physicist. Edith Anne Stoney (6 January 1869 – 25 June 1938) was an Irish physicist.
Caused by mutations in any of sixteen genes that weaken the skin's structural attachment layers, this rare inherited condition causes painful blistering from the slightest friction — which disease?
Epidermolysis bullosa: Rare medical conditions that result in easy blistering of the skin and mucous membranes.
This small woodland bird has blue-gray upperparts, a black eye-stripe, and famously plasters the entrance to its tree-hole nest with mud if it's too large — what is it?
Eurasian nuthatch: Small passerine bird species.
Reproducing via spores rather than seeds or flowers, this group of vascular plants unfurls from coiled 'fiddleheads' into fronds and numbers over 10,000 species — what are they?
Fern: Class of vascular plants. The group includes about 10,560 known extant species.
With atomic number 87 and a most stable isotope whose half-life is just 22 minutes, this alkali metal is the second-rarest naturally occurring element on Earth — which one?
Francium: Chemical element with atomic number 87 (Fr)

Published by Einstein in 1916 as a refinement of Newton's law of gravitation, this geometric framework describes gravity as curved spacetime, summed up by Wheeler as 'space-time tells matter how to move; matter tells space-time how to curve'?
General relativity: Theory of gravitation as curved spacetime. The relation is specified by the Einstein field equations, a system of second-order partial differential equations.
Despite its common name, this Eurasian wolf-like canid is more closely related to wolves and coyotes than to its African namesakes — what animal is it?
Born Herman Mudgett and dubbed the 'Beast of Chicago,' this con artist and serial killer worked his most notorious crimes around the 1893 World's Columbian Exposition — who was he?
H. H. Holmes: American con artist and serial killer (1861–1896)
Dubbed 'the Gauss of modern mathematics,' this French polymath's work on the three-body problem uncovered the first chaotic deterministic system, laying the groundwork for chaos theory — who is he?
Henri Poincaré: French mathematician, physicist and engineer (1854–1912)
With red compound eyes set wider apart in females, this insect lays batches of about 100 eggs on decaying matter that hatch into maggots — which species?
Housefly: Species of insect. The housefly (Musca domestica) is a fly of the suborder Cyclorrhapha.
Distinguished by the male's large, transversely ridged curved horns, which wild goat species roams Eurasia and Africa?
This order of crustaceans includes both seafaring gribbles and the woodlice in your garden, with females brooding their young in a belly pouch called a marsupium. What is it?
Isopoda: Order of arthropods. The order is divided into eleven suborders.
As Grand Pensionary of Holland during the Dutch Golden Age, this statesman dominated politics from 1650 until the 'Disaster Year' of 1672 — who was he?
This Hungarian-American biochemist spent years fighting skepticism over messenger RNA before her groundwork made mRNA vaccines possible, earning a shared 2023 Nobel Prize — who is she?
Commonly called the voice box, which organ in the upper neck houses the vocal cords and protects the windpipe from food entering it?
Larynx: Voice box, an organ in the neck of amphibians, reptiles, and mammals.
The only person ever to win two unshared Nobel Prizes, this American chemist earned one for his work on the chemical bond and another for peace activism — who is he?
Linus Pauling: American scientist and activist (1901–1994)
This American experimental physicist won the 1968 Nobel Prize for discovering resonance states using the hydrogen bubble chamber — who was he?
Luis Walter Alvarez: American physicist, inventor and professor (1911–1988)

Often called the mirror image of depression, this psychiatric state brings racing thoughts, pressured speech, boundless energy, and a shrinking need for sleep — what is this elevated mood syndrome called?
Mania: State of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.
Isolated in 1958 from cow pineal glands because it could lighten frog skin, this nighttime brain hormone turned out to be the body's regulator of the sleep-wake cycle — what is it?
Melatonin: Hormone released by the pineal gland.
Which Hungarian-American psychologist coined the term 'flow' to describe a highly focused, creative mental state?

The tallest and heaviest living species of deer, this Northern Hemisphere giant is topped in North American body mass only by the bison, and its males sport broad, hand-shaped antlers unlike any other deer's pointed racks. What is it?
Moose: Largest species of deer. It is also the tallest, and the second-largest, land animal in North America, falling short only to the American bison in body mass.
Sold as Narcan, this opioid antagonist can restore breathing within minutes of an overdose but may trigger sudden withdrawal in opioid-dependent people — what is it?
Naloxone: Opioid receptor antagonist. Naloxone, sold under the brand name Narcan among others, is an opioid antagonist, a medication used to reverse or reduce the effects of opioids.
Discovered in 1846 by Ascanio Sobrero, this oily explosive liquid became the key ingredient in dynamite — what is it?

The most widely cultivated species of its genus, this bulb vegetable counts garlic, leeks and chives among its close relatives, and the shallot was reclassified as merely a variety of it in 2011 — what is it?
Onion: Bulbous vegetable. The shallot is a botanical variety of the onion which was classified as a separate species until 2011.
Nicknamed the 'scaly anteater,' this nocturnal mammal is covered in keratin scales and slurps up ants and termites with a long tongue — which animal?
Pangolin: Mammals of the order Pholidota.
This genus of fungi is responsible for both a groundbreaking antibiotic and the mold that ripens certain blue cheeses — which genus?
Known across South Asia as Indian gooseberry or amla, this deciduous tree is native to tropical regions of the continent — which plant?
Phyllanthus emblica: Berry and plant. Phyllanthus emblica, commonly known as emblic, Indian gooseberry, amalaki, amloki, or amla, is a deciduous tree of the family Phyllanthaceae.

The most common hormonal disorder in women of reproductive age, it's diagnosed by two of three signs — irregular periods, high testosterone, or many antral follicles — despite a name that misleadingly implies true cysts. What's its newer name?
Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: Hormonal disorder in women. The exact cause of PMOS remains uncertain.
This Old World tree species has two main cultivar groups, the dark-red Morello and the lighter Amarelle, prized for their tart, edible pulp — which fruit-bearing plant?
Prunus cerasus: Species of cherry tree. Prunus cerasus (sour cherry, tart cherry, or dwarf cherry) is an Old World species of Prunus in the subgenus Cerasus (cherries).
A small herbivore of the family Leporidae and a cousin to hares, this prey animal has been introduced to every continent except Antarctica — what is it?
Rabbit: Mammals of the family Leporidae. The most widespread rabbit genera are Oryctolagus and Sylvilagus.
Responsible for at least half of all common colds, this tiny RNA virus in the Picornaviridae family measures only about 30 nanometers across — what is it?
Discovered in 1844 by Karl Ernst Claus and named in honor of Russia, which unreactive platinum-group element with atomic number 44 now caps extreme ultraviolet photomasks for chip lithography?
Ruthenium: Chemical element with atomic number 44 (Ru)
Exceeding 30 centimeters in length, this centipede from South America is the largest of its kind, preying on animals as large as small mammals and reptiles — which species?

Scolopendra gigantea: Species of Chilopoda (centipede). Scolopendra gigantea, also known as the Peruvian giant yellow-leg centipede or Amazonian giant centipede, is a centipede in the genus Scolopendra.
Named for its enormous footwear-shaped beak, this large wading bird of East African swamps was once classified with storks but is now grouped with pelicans and herons — what is it?
Shoebill: Species of bird. The shoebill (Balaeniceps rex), also known as the whale-headed stork, whalebill, and shoe-billed stork, is a large long-legged wading bird.
This frozen dessert blends ice with fruit juice or purée — and sometimes wine, liqueur, or honey — for a refreshing icy treat. What is it called?
Sorbet: Frozen dessert. Sorbet is a frozen dessert made using ice combined with fruit juice, fruit purée, or other ingredients, such as wine, liqueur, or honey.
Whose pure-white winter coat became 'ermine,' the prized fur trimming the ceremonial robes of the UK House of Lords — and which was disastrously introduced to New Zealand? What animal is it?
Sometimes called gadflies, the females of this fly family bite land animals, including humans, to get the blood protein they need to produce eggs — which family?
Tabanidae: Family of insects. Horse flies and deer flies are true flies in the family Tabanidae in the insect order Diptera.
Native to the tropical Americas, this small evergreen tree's fermented seeds become cocoa powder, cocoa butter, and chocolate — which tree?
Theobroma cacao: Species of tree grown for its seeds.
Located at either side of the back of your throat, these paired lymphoid organs form part of a defensive ring guarding the entrance to your digestive and respiratory tracts — what are they?

Tonsil: Lymphoid organs in the mouth and throat. The palatine tonsils and the adenoid tonsil are organs consisting of lymphoepithelial tissue located near the oropharynx and nasopharynx (parts of the throat).
Renowned as the greatest astronomer before the invention of the telescope, this Dane noticed an unexpectedly bright new star in 1572 and devoted himself to ever more precise instruments. Who was he?
This legume, also called the broad bean, can trigger a dangerous reaction called favism in people with a certain metabolic blood disorder — what species is it?
Vicia faba: Species of plant in the pea and bean family.
One of the widest-ranging mammals on Earth, this adaptable suid native to Eurasia and North Africa has turned invasive wherever people introduced it — what is it?
This French mathematician and physicist wrote Institutions de Physique, a work translated into German and Italian that sparked heated 18th-century debate — who is she?
Émilie du Châtelet: French mathematician, physicist, and author (1706–1749)
Lawrencium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for lawrencium is Lr. Lawrencium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lr and atomic number 103.

Who among these is a comedian?
Mirco Nontschew is a comedian. Mirco Nontschew (29 October 1969 – c. 3 December 2021) was a German comedian.
In what year was Vanessa Hudgens born?
Vanessa Hudgens: Vanessa Anne Hudgens ( HUJ-ənz; born December 14, 1988) is an American actress and singer.
In what year was Ewan McGregor born?
Ewan McGregor: Ewan Gordon McGregor ( YOO-ən; born 31 March 1971) is a Scottish actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Matt LeBlanc born?
Matt LeBlanc: Matthew Steven LeBlanc ( lə-BLAHNK; born July 25, 1967) is an American actor.
In what year was Mckenna Grace born?
Mckenna Grace (born June 25, 2006) is an American actress and singer.
In what year was Morena Baccarin born?
Morena Baccarin: Morena Silva de Vaz Setta Baccarin (Brazilian Portuguese: [moˈɾenɐ bakaˈɾĩ]; born June 2, 1979) is an American actress.
In what year was Danny DeVito born?
Danny DeVito: Daniel Michael DeVito Jr., ( də-VEE-toh; born November 17, 1944) is an American actor and filmmaker.
In what year was Jason Momoa born?
Jason Momoa: Joseph Jason Namakaeha Momoa (born August 1, 1979) is an American actor and film producer.
In what year was Emma Watson born?
Emma Watson: Emma Charlotte Duerre Watson (born 15 April 1990) is an English actress.
In what year was Maya Hawke born?
Maya Hawke: Maya Ray Thurman Hawke (born July 8, 1998) is an American actress and singer-songwriter.
